faq: Which platforms can you move from?
WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, Shopify, Weebly and hand-coded sites are all common. Send the link and tell us the platform, and we confirm what can move automatically and what we rebuild by hand.
Will I lose my Google rankings?

We cannot promise rankings, but we protect them as far as we can: same page addresses where possible, 301 redirects for every changed address, and titles and meta text copied over. Small dips after a move are normal and usually settle.
Does my old site go offline?

Not until you say so. We build on a Webflow staging address while your current site stays live. When you approve, we switch the domain, which takes minutes, and you keep the old site as a fallback for a while.
Can you move an online store too?
Webflow Ecommerce is a different job from this page. For a store we quote the product and order move separately, so tell us in the order form if shop pages are part of the site.

desc:
Website migration to Webflow moves your existing site, whether WordPress, Wix, Squarespace or hand-coded, into a clean Webflow project. Ecom Swift LLC carries over pages, images and posts, sets up redirects and checks everything before the switch.

## What is a website migration to Webflow?

A migration to Webflow means rebuilding your current site inside Webflow while keeping the content, structure and addresses that already work. Text, images, blog posts and page titles are carried across. The layout is recreated with Webflow's Designer, so it uses clean structure rather than an imported mess.

It is not a copy and paste of code. Each platform stores content differently, so the work is mapping what you have to what Webflow needs: pages, collections, forms and settings.

## Why the move needs a plan, not just a rebuild

The biggest risk in any migration is losing the traffic you already have. If old addresses stop working, visitors land on error pages and search engines drop the links they have stored. A new design on top of broken redirects can undo years of visibility.

A second risk is a gap in service. A site that goes offline while the new one is built costs enquiries and credibility. A good migration keeps the old site live until the new one is tested and ready.

## How a careful move protects traffic and trust

Redirects are the heart of it. A 301 redirect tells browsers and search engines that an old address now lives at a new one, so visitors and link value follow along. Mapping every old address to the right new page, and testing the list, keeps that path open.

Titles, meta descriptions, alt text and heading structure also move across. Keeping them in place means search engines see familiar content on a faster, cleaner site. Results can still shift after any move, but a careful migration removes the avoidable causes.

## What a good migration includes

- A full inventory of existing pages, posts, images and forms.
- Text and images carried over with their titles and meta descriptions.
- Layouts rebuilt in Webflow, responsive on desktop, tablet and phone.
- Blog posts or repeating content moved into CMS collections.
- A redirect map from every old address to its new one.
- 301 redirects set up in Webflow and tested.
- Forms reconnected to your inbox or tools.
- Image compression and alt text carried across.
- Domain switch support, with the old site live until approval.
- A guide for resubmitting your sitemap in Search Console.

## How we run the move

We begin with a crawl of your current site and a list of everything to move. Then we build the new pages in your Webflow workspace, check them against the original and prepare the redirect list. You review the site on a staging address before any domain change.

The Basic package moves a small brochure site, with text and images carried over, a redirect list and forms reconnected. The Standard package moves a fuller site with blog posts into the CMS, tested 301 redirects, titles and meta copied across and domain switch support. The Premium package handles a larger site with imported CMS items, a mapped old structure, image compression, alt text and a Search Console guide, plus a period of fixes after launch. Extra pages, blog image re-optimization and a post-move redirect audit are available as add-ons.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep your old site online until we confirm the new one is ready.
- Send a list of the pages that matter most.
- Give us access to your domain settings when the switch is due.
- Back up your old content before work begins.
- Check your key pages after launch.

**Avoid:**
- Cancelling the old hosting too early.
- Changing page addresses without a redirect.
- Rebuilding stale content in Webflow simply because it was on the old site.
- Switching the domain on a day you cannot monitor it.
- Expecting stores and complex membership features to move automatically.

## Who this service is for

This service suits owners outgrowing a template-based builder, businesses with a WordPress site that has become slow or hard to maintain, and anyone who wants a design they can control without plugin upkeep. Online stores are a different scale of project, so tell us what you sell and we will advise honestly.

## What we need from you

Send your current site address, a list of key pages and the login method your platform allows for a collaborator or staff user. We never need your password. Domain changes are done in your registrar account, and we guide you through each step.
